# Companies Act 2013 - valuation provisions (synthetic extract)

## Section 247 - Valuation by Registered Valuer
Where a valuation of shares or assets is required, it shall be made by a Registered Valuer (RV) who is independent of the company and the transaction parties.

## Valuation report content
The report shall state:
- the valuation date and the methodology used (discounted cash flow, net asset value, or market multiples) and the reasons for choosing it,
- key assumptions, and
- the fair value per share.

## Validity
A valuation report is valid for **90 days** from the valuation date. A transaction completed after that period requires a fresh or refreshed report.

## Penalty
A Registered Valuer who knowingly makes a false or misleading valuation shall be punishable with a fine of not less than Rs 1 lakh and up to Rs 5 lakh.

## Use under other laws
A valuation report by a Registered Valuer under this Act is accepted as evidence of fair value for pricing of share transfers under FEMA and for establishing that a transfer is a bona fide commercial transaction under foreign contribution rules.

## Registration and account
An association or trust may receive foreign contribution only if it holds an FCRA registration, and only into its designated FCRA bank account.

## Foreign source
A foreign company, including a company incorporated outside India such as a Singapore entity, is a foreign source.

## Commercial consideration exception
Money received from a foreign source as **bona fide commercial consideration** (for example the price for shares sold) is **not** foreign contribution, provided that:
1. the price is supported by a valuation report of a **Registered Valuer** under the Companies Act 2013, which must be valid on the date of transfer, and
2. the transaction is reported to the authorities within 30 days.
Where these conditions are not met, the receipt is treated as foreign contribution and requires prior permission, failing which the registration may be cancelled.

## Utilisation
Foreign contribution may be used only for the purposes stated in the registration, and administrative expenses are capped at 20%.

# Notification SYN-NTF/1/2025: Withholding on Royalty Payments to Non-Residents under Section 94Y

## 1. Scope and Applicability
This notification applies to every Indian resident payer who credits or pays royalty to a non-resident payee in a financial year, whether by cash transfer, adjustment against an intercompany account, or release from an escrow arrangement. Payments for the transfer of rights in a copyrighted article are included.

## 2. Rate and Threshold
Tax shall be withheld at 12 per cent of the gross royalty where the aggregate royalty credited to a single non-resident payee during the financial year exceeds Rs 25 lakh. Once the threshold is crossed, withholding applies to the entire royalty amount credited in that year, not merely the excess.

## 3. Deposit and Filing
Tax withheld shall be deposited with the designated government account by the seventh day of the month following the month of deduction. The payer shall furnish the quarterly statement in the prescribed form within 30 days from the end of each quarter.

## 4. Indemnity and Escrow Holdbacks
Where the payee disputes the applicable rate, the payer may hold the disputed portion in an escrow account for up to 90 days pending a lower-deduction certificate. Any indemnity given to the payee for tax not withheld must be disclosed in the payer's audit file.

## 5. Consequences of Default
Failure to deduct attracts simple interest at 1 per cent per month from the date of deduction to the date of deposit. A penalty equal to the amount not deducted may be levied. This notification takes effect from 1 April 2026; payments under contracts executed before 1 October 2025 remain governed by the earlier regime.

Incomplete applications are returned once, with a 30-day window to cure defects. Failure to cure attracts rejection without refund of the fee. Withdrawal after admission, without the Authority's consent, attracts a penalty of 2% of the transaction value, subject to a cap of Rs 5 lakh.

Where turnover exceeds the ceiling during a year, the person ceases to be eligible from the day the threshold is crossed and must pay tax at normal rates on stock held. The deductor shall deposit the tax by the 7th of the following month and file Form 27Z quarterly with the Tax Authority.

## 3. Consequences of default
- Interest under Section 94Z(5) at 1.5% per month on tax not withheld, from the date it was deductible until deposit.
- Penalty under Section 271Z equal to 100% of the tax not withheld.

## 4. Related instruments
The meaning of "cross-border technical and consultancy services" is further clarified in CBDT Circular SYN-CBDT-C/07/2025.

# Circular No. SYN-CBDT-C/07/2025 (dated 20 August 2025)

Issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to remove doubts on the scope of Section 94Z of the Income Tax Act (synthetic), as amended by Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025.

## 1. Clarification (retrospective)
It is clarified that "cross-border technical and consultancy services" under Section 94Z always included intra-group management service charges, shared-service recharges and cost-sharing recoveries paid to associated non-resident enterprises.
This is a **retrospective clarification** and has effect from 1 April 2023, the date Section 94Z was introduced. It is not a new levy.

## 2. Consequence
Deductors who did not withhold on intra-group management charges in FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 are liable to withhold at the rate then applicable (5%), together with interest at 1.5% per month under Section 94Z(5).

## 3. Penalty relief
Penalty under Section 271Z shall not be levied where the shortfall tax and interest are deposited on or before 31 March 2026.
After that date penalty equal to 100% of the tax not withheld applies.

## 4. Distinction from the Notification
Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025 (10% rate, Rs 50 lakh threshold) operates prospectively from 1 April 2025. This Circular clarifies scope only; it does not change the rate for earlier years.

CBIC Circular SYN-CBIC/203/2025 - Input Service Distributor (ISD) Registration and Credit Distribution

# Circular No. SYN-CBIC/203/2025 (dated 3 March 2025)

Issued by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) on distribution of input tax credit on common input services.

## 1. Mandatory ISD registration
With effect from 1 April 2025 (prospective), any registered person that wishes to distribute input tax credit on common input services (for example head-office audit, IT or management services) to its branches or distinct persons must obtain registration as an Input Service Distributor (ISD) under Rule 39A.

## 2. ISD invoice
Credit may be distributed only through an ISD invoice issued by the ISD. Distribution by ordinary invoice, journal entry or internal debit note is not valid.

## 3. Consequences of non-compliance
- Credit distributed without ISD registration or ISD invoice is denied to the recipient unit.
- Recovery of wrongly availed credit with interest at 18% per annum.
- Penalty of Rs 25,000 per instance.

## 4. Interaction with e-invoicing
ISD invoices are subject to the e-invoicing regime. See the ruling of the 57th GST Council for the date from which ISD invoices must carry an Invoice Reference Number (IRN).

57th GST Council Ruling - E-Invoicing Threshold and ISD Invoices
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT FOR BENCHMARKING. NOT AN OFFICIAL COUNCIL RECORD. All thresholds and dates are fictional.

# Ruling of the 57th GST Council Meeting

## 1. E-invoicing threshold (prospective)
E-invoicing becomes mandatory for every registered person whose Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) exceeds Rs 5 crore, down from Rs 10 crore, with effect from 1 January 2026.

## 2. Invoice Reference Number and QR code
Every e-invoice must carry an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) generated on the Invoice Registration Portal, and a QR code. Invoices without an IRN are not valid for claiming input tax credit by the recipient.

## 3. ISD invoices
ISD invoices issued under Circular SYN-CBIC/203/2025 for distribution of input tax credit must also carry an IRN and QR code from 1 January 2026.

## 4. Reporting window
Taxpayers with AATO of Rs 10 crore and above must report invoices to the portal within 30 days of the invoice date.

## 5. Penalty
Failure to issue an e-invoice attracts a penalty of 100% of the tax due or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, per invoice.

CBDT Circular SYN-CBDT-C/11/2026 - Section 94W Director Sitting Fees
SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT FOR BENCHMARKING. Fictional section numbers, rates and dates.
CBDT Circular No. SYN-CBDT-C/11/2026 (dated 9 February 2026)
The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) clarifies the operation of Section 94W of the Income Tax Act (synthetic) on
tax withheld from sitting fees paid to company directors.
1. Rate and threshold (prospective)
With effect from 1 April 2026, a company shall withhold tax at 8% on sitting fees and commission paid to a director in a
financial year where the aggregate exceeds Rs 2 lakh. The provision applies only to payments made on or after 1 April
2026.
2. Independent directors
Sitting fees paid to independent directors who are non-resident are subject to the same 8% rate and the Rs 2 lakh
threshold. There is no lower treaty rate unless the director furnishes a tax residency certificate by 30 April of the
following year.
3. Reimbursement of expenses
Reimbursement of actual travel and lodging costs supported by invoices is not sitting fees and is outside Section 94W.
4. Default
Interest at 1.25% per month applies on tax not withheld. Penalty under Section 271W equals 50% of the tax not
withheld.
5. Filing
Withholding under Section 94W shall be reported in Form 26W by the 15th day after the end of each quarter.
